Date: 2027-06-21T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow up: token volumes & peak TPS from today's call

Thanks for the call today — quick recap and numbers from our end so you can size pricing:

- Core usage: chat summaries and search re-rank
- Expected steady-state: 180M tokens / month (input+output)
- Peak TPS (30-min windows): ~75 TPS sustained, occasional short spikes to 140 TPS (1-2 min)
- Typical request size: 800 tokens average (incl. context & response)
- Budget target: roughly $8k–$15k / month to start; CFO wants options under $20k

I've attached a rough usage CSV. Can you confirm expected $/1M token bands and whether Redwood's hosted plan supports our peak without large overage risk? Also curious about canary/auto-fallback options if capacity constrained.

Happy to jump on another 20-min slot but wanted the numbers in writing.

Best,
Alice Park
Head of AI Product
NimbleHealth

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-22T09:03:00-07:00

Thanks Alice — great context and the CSV helps. A few clarifying q's before we lock a slab:

1) The 180M tokens/month — is that an average month or first‑year steady state? If it's early-stage, do you expect growth to ~300M in 6–12 months?
2) When you say 140 TPS spikes, are those full-token spikes (i.e., concurrent long responses) or short control calls? Any percent of traffic that hits the >1k token response range?
3) Can you share the percentage split between interactive chat (low-latency) vs asynchronous bulk calls (higher latency ok)?

Quick answers from our side to your asks:
- Unit economics: for hosted API we typically present tiered $/1M token bands. Rough starting guidance (non-binding): $900–$1,200 per 1M for small pilot slabs (~50–200M), $650–$800 per 1M for committed slabs >200M, and custom pricing for >1B.
- Peak handling: with our hosted routing and autoscaling we can support bursts to 140 TPS if you take a committed slab or enable burst capacity (extra fees for sustained bursts). Without commit there is higher chance of fallback to a compatible model variant in extreme congestion.
- Canary/fallback: yes — we can configure an A/B rollout and automatic fallback to a smaller model with comparable quality as a safety net.

Next steps I propose:
- Send us a short confirmation of whether 180M is steady vs ramping.
- If steady, we can put together a 2‑option commercial: (A) 6‑month pilot (50–200M slab) with a pilot unit price and credit for overage; (B) annual commit for 200–400M with lower $/1M.
- I'll include an estimated cost worksheet and a sample SOW/terms you can share with procurement.

Looping in Karthik for peak capacity notes.

Best,
Irene
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi all — adding technical pricing/ops color.

- If average request size is ~800 tokens and peak concurrency is 140 TPS, sustained long responses during spikes are the cost driver. For sizing we account for both token burn and concurrent KV cache/memory footprint.
- Recommendation: if NimbleHealth expects >100 TPS peaks regularly, include a 'burst reserve' of ~60% above committed concurrency to avoid throttles. That means for a 180M monthly baseline we would recommend a 250M commit slab for safe headroom if peaks are regular.
- Price examples (hosted):
  * Pilot slab (50–150M): $1,050 per 1M
  * Mid commit (200–350M): $720 per 1M
  * Reserve/overflow pricing: +25% on per‑token rate for metered bursts

Irene — I attached a quick worksheet and a sample hosted pricing PDF; Alice — happy to run through numbers live and map to your budget target. If procurement wants a single line unit price for modeling: use $750/1M as a conservative estimate for a ~250M commit.

Karthik

- Traffic split: ~70% interactive low-latency chat, ~30% async batch scoring.

If you can get the quote and SOW by EOD Friday I'll share with our CFO and legal.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — happy to hop on 30m tomorrow if you prefer.
